cohort: The study included 9,096,788 pregnancies, of which 25,044 were in pregnant women with epilepsy, from the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (HCUP-NIS) database between 2004-2014.
finding: Pregnant women with epilepsy have a significantly higher risk of nearly every pregnancy, delivery, and neonatal complication investigated, including maternal death and intrauterine fetal demise.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with epilepsy were more likely to undergo cesarean section (adjusted OR: 1.29, 95% CI: 1.25-1.33).
followup_time: Up to neonatal outcomes, generally within the delivery hospitalization period
